component_records.title: Project management, governance and MoDOT coordination
component_records.description: We run the study as a single managed programme under a named Principal Investigator who is the Offeror's primary contact, with a Work Plan of no more than ten pages at 12-point minimum that covers every Section 2 item and expressly recognises MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve the work plans (R083). We facilitate the kick-off meeting with MoDOT to review work plan, scope and schedule and to establish the protocol for regular ongoing communications and coordination with the team (R047), and we develop minutes for the kick-off and for each quarterly status meeting (R049). We submit quarterly updates on work accomplished on or before the last working day of March, June, September and December for the duration of the project (R030), and we maintain monthly e-mail and phone communications with MoDOT contacts giving ongoing progress updates (R033). We schedule the interim presentation near the mid-point of the project to update MoDOT on progress and project direction (R032), and we make advice and information on matters covered by the Agreement available to the Construction and Materials Division as the work progresses (R105). The plan is baselined on a 15-month contract period (R017) and is re-confirmed at kick-off so that MoDOT's approvals, not our assumptions, set the dates. All project meetings, presentations and calls we schedule are held between 7:30 a.m. and 4 p.m. Central time (R018), and the schedule is built so that every deliverable lands on its stated date, because time is of the essence under the RFP (R006).

component_records.title: Milestone schedule and deliverable calendar
component_records.description: We deliver against a single milestone calendar that fixes the kick-off meeting on 11/15/2024 to discuss project requirements and deliverables (R035), the Data Management Plan on 12/4/2024 (R036), the presentation on 4/25/2025 of how the AI/ML will create draft LLDs with MoDOT feedback for improvement (R037), the interim presentation completed by 9/15/2025 (R039), the draft final report, summary report and user manual on 11/3/2025 (R040), and the final report, summary report, presentation and user manual on 1/1/2026 (R042), with the final invoice due and the contract ending 2/2/2026 (R044). We also hold the draft documents to the requirement that they reach MoDOT approximately two months before the final report (R041), which the 11/3/2025 and 1/1/2026 dates satisfy, and we treat the draft Synthesis Report and Research Summary as final products except for revisions based on MoDOT's review (R061). The calendar is published in the Work Plan and tracked weekly, with each milestone shown as a MoDOT acceptance point, and every scheduled meeting, presentation and submission event is set within the 7:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. Central window (R018).

component_records.title: Data management plan and research data handling
component_records.description: We submit a Data Management Plan to MoDOT within two weeks after the project kick-off meeting (R051), which also lands on the 12/4/2024 date in the schedule. The DMP describes the anticipated format(s) our data and related files will use (R052) and commits to platform-independent, non-proprietary formats so the data retains maximum future utility for MoDOT (R053). It also records the storage location, retention and access rules for MoDOT-supplied LLD examples and any derived training data, and it is written so that no Personal Identifiable Information is held in any database table without a specific business need approved by the IS Cyber Security Team (R149).

component_records.title: Literature review of state DOT AI/ML right-of-way practice
component_records.description: We conduct a thorough literature search and review of other state DOT practices using AI/ML for right-of-way purposes (R054), covering peer-reviewed research, state DOT research reports and published ROW automation practice, and we deliver it as a structured review with a comparison matrix of use cases, methods, data sources and reported outcomes. The review is positioned as the evidence base for the research question — whether AI/ML can usefully produce a first draft LLD from MHTC parameters (R016) — and its findings feed the design of the proof of concept rather than sitting as a standalone document.

component_records.title: LLD drafting engine: program selection, build and MoDOT IS approval
component_records.description: We name the program used to develop the LLDs and submit it to MoDOT Information Systems for approval before any proof-of-concept work begins, so that Task 3c cannot start until that approval is in hand (R056). The drafting capability is built only on technologies approved in the RFP's Approved Technologies section (R134), using a currently supported .NET 6.0 or above release unless a specific need for .NET Framework is demonstrated, in which case a currently supported 4.8 release or above is used (R135, R136), with web applications on MVC, Razor Pages or Web API (R137). Python 3.x from python.org is used for ESRI scripting and small one-time utilities, with any large-scale use put to the BRPT for approval (R142), and library dependencies are reviewed and updated annually (R138). No third-party tool or software that would place a licensing responsibility on MoDOT is introduced without prior BRPT and IS management review and approval (R139). The engine encodes the drafting rules the RFP requires: descriptions meeting MoDOT EPG Section 236.4.6.2 (R012), deed-exact wording where a property is acquired in its entirety (R014), and explicit recital of the specific rights acquired, conveyed or leased where those rights are less than fee simple title (R015).

component_records.title: Proof of concept: draft LLD generation and MoDOT review loop
component_records.description: We demonstrate how our technology creates draft legal land descriptions for a variety of properties (R057), running the demonstration on the MoDOT-provided LLD examples and on additional property types agreed with Right of Way staff, and we present the results on 4/25/2025 with MoDOT providing feedback for improvement (R037). Each cycle produces draft LLDs, a side-by-side comparison against the surveyor-reviewed source descriptions, and a written log of the corrections MoDOT made, which is fed back into the model and the drafting rules. A professional land surveyor on the team reviews every generated description to confirm the parcel corresponds with the right of way plans and that those plans correspond with survey information, mirroring the review MoDOT requires before a deed is presented to a grantor. The proof of concept closes with a documented finding on the usefulness of AI/ML for first-draft LLDs from MHTC parameters (R016).

component_records.title: Training and user manual for Right of Way staff
component_records.description: Once the system is developed and finalized we provide training to Right of Way staff (R058) and supply a user manual for staff to reference (R059). Training is delivered as instructor-led sessions plus recorded walkthroughs, with a hands-on exercise in which staff generate a draft LLD, review and edit it, and export it, and the user manual is delivered in editable and print-ready form covering setup, the drafting workflow, review and edit steps, and troubleshooting. Both are delivered in draft with the 11/3/2025 package and finalized with the 1/1/2026 package, and the manual is maintained through the final acceptance period so staff are trained on the version they will actually use.

component_records.title: Reporting: draft and final reports, research summary and presentation
component_records.description: We deliver a draft Synthesis Report and Research Summary that are final products except for revisions based on MoDOT's review (R061), submitted on 11/3/2025 and approximately two months ahead of the final report (R041). We then deliver a final report detailing the tasks completed during the project and including all findings generated during its duration (R064), a 1-2 page research summary stating the project objectives, findings and conclusions (R065), and a presentation for MoDOT staff summarizing the important or significant details of the project (R066), all by 1/1/2026. Reports follow the Publication Guidelines and summary template obtained from the MoDOT information-researchers page, and the final package is submitted with the final invoice on 2/2/2026 (R044).

component_records.title: Application compliance: accessibility, hosting and security
component_records.description: Any web application we deliver meets the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard based on Section 508 as amended (R151) and conforms to WCAG 2.1 at 'AA' level (R152), verified by automated and manual testing before each release. It runs in a modern browser with no client-side software such as Java Applets or Silverlight (R146), and is tested and designed against the latest IS-approved browsers (R144). On-premise database deployments run on Oracle 19C (R147), with SQL Server used only where MoDOT IS Data Service Management approves it (R148), and no Personal Identifiable Information is stored in any database table without a specific business need approved by the IS Cyber Security Team (R149). We use no text, diagrams, photographs, audio, multimedia, source code, script or graphics from another author's web pages unless the author explicitly permits free copying or appropriate arrangements are made (R153), and no vendor logos, branding or other company endorsements appear in the application where a supported, licensed option exists to remove them (R154).

component_records.title: Contract, compliance and insurance obligations
component_records.description: We accept the contract provisions stated in the RFP as they will appear in the post-award negotiated contract (R102) and accept that MHTC may cancel the award and select a different Offeror if the parties cannot agree on post-award terms (R103); we also accept that written clarifications issued by MHTC govern over conflicting requirements in the RFP or in our proposal (R109). We do not release any material or report we prepare to the public without the prior consent of MHTC's representative (R106) and we notify MHTC immediately of any request for confidential information (R126). We do not assign, delegate or novate any interest in the services without MHTC's prior written consent (R107), and we remain ultimately responsible and liable to MHTC for the complete, accurate and professional quality and performance of the services regardless of subcontractors or suppliers (R114). We include the provisions of Section (3), paragraph I of the Agreement in every subcontract (R117) and we seek MBE and WBE participation through subcontractors, suppliers and joint ventures targeting 10% MBE and 5% WBE (R113). We comply with Missouri Executive Order 07-13 on not employing individuals ineligible to work in the United States (R115), and we affirm by sworn affidavit and documentation our enrolment and participation in a federal work authorization program such as E-Verify for employees working on the contract (R119), provide the completed E-Verify Memorandum of Understanding for those employees (R120), affirm by sworn affidavit that we do not knowingly employ any unauthorized alien in connection with the contracted services (R121), and participate in the federal work authorization programme to verify employment eligibility of newly hired employees working on MHTC-contracted services (R157). Where the Offeror is a sole proprietorship or partnership, each sole proprietor and general partner provides affirmative proof of lawful presence under Section 208.009, RSMo (R122). All documents, reports, exhibits and other deliverables we produce at MHTC's direction, and information supplied by MHTC, remain MHTC property (R124), and we make our records available at no charge to MHTC and the Missouri State Auditor at all reasonable times during the Agreement and for three years from final payment (R128). We carry General Liability of not less than $500,000 per person and $3,000,000 per occurrence (R131), Automobile Liability of not less than $500,000 per person and $3,000,000 per occurrence (R132), and a Missouri State Workmen's Compensation policy or equivalent in accordance with state law (R133), and we will provide certificates of insurance on request before contract signing (R130). We also accept that MHTC's representative may reproduce and use products derived from our work without payment of royalties or fees (R129).

component_records.title: Pricing, cost estimate and proposal responsiveness
component_records.description: We price the whole Scope of Work within a total not to exceed $175,000 (R045) and submit a proposed cost estimate covering all services defined in the Scope of Work (R096) on Section (4), the Price Page (R097), broken out into Salaries, Benefits, Operating Expense, Facilities and Administration (F&A) Cost, Miscellaneous and a Total (R100), with every miscellaneous cost itemized on an additional sheet where needed (R101). The estimate is quoted for the full 15-month term rather than per year, and the Price Page template is obtained from the MoDOT information-researchers page and completed in its prescribed format. We submit as a qualified organisation — a private consultant, university or research organisation — proposing to conduct the TR202504 study for MHTC and MoDOT (R005, R011), and we submit a proposal that is acceptable to MHTC without further clarification (R108).

component_records.title: RFP communications and submission discipline
component_records.description: We manage all contact with MoDOT through the single designated channel, submitting our questions and comments to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by the date and time listed in section 1E (R077) and making no contact with MoDOT employees by any other method. We respond to the RFP within the stated submission deadlines, treating time as of the essence (R006): the proposal is filed by the stated due date and time, and every subsequent deliverable is tracked against its contractual date with escalation inside our team if a date is at risk. All RFP events we attend or convene — clarification calls, the kick-off, quarterly status meetings, the 4/25/2025 demonstration, the interim presentation and the final presentation — are scheduled between 7:30 a.m. and 4 p.m. Central time (R018), and we confirm the exact question deadline and submission deadline with MoDOT through the designated email before relying on them.

items.text: The Missouri Highways and Transportation Commission (MHTC) is the issuing body, and the Missouri Department of Transportation (MoDOT) is the beneficiary, with MoDOT's Right of Way staff reviewing draft legal land descriptions.
The work is coordinated by the Research Unit of MoDOT's Construction and Materials Division, and the Offeror must fully coordinate its activities with that Division.

MoDOT's Right of Way staff must describe realty rights acquired or conveyed by MHTC using the metes and bounds method unless a property is acquired in its entirety, in which case the description must be written exactly as it appears on the last deed of record.
Every property description prepared on behalf of MHTC must meet the requirements of MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide (EPG) Section 236.4.6.2.

Before a general warranty deed, quitclaim deed or similar document is presented to the grantor, a professional land surveyor must review the property description to verify the parcel corresponds with the right of way plans and that those plans correspond with survey information gathered by the surveyor.
Writing these legal land descriptions is long and tedious work, which is the pain point driving the RFP.

The business driver is to determine the usefulness of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) for producing a "first draft" of the legal land description (LLD) from MHTC parameters that MoDOT Right of Way staff could then review and edit.

MoDOT operates on a fiscal year running from July 1 to June 30, and quarterly project updates feed the Statewide Planning and Research (SPR) Quarterly Report the Construction and Materials Division submits to FHWA each quarter.

MoDOT wants a research study, TR202504 "Using AI/ML to Write Legal Land Descriptions," that determines whether AI/ML can generate a first draft of a legal land description for review and editing by Right of Way staff.

The scope comprises six tasks: Task 1 Project Management, Task 2 Literature Review, Task 3a/3b/3c (MoDOT-provided LLD examples, Offeror naming its program, and a proof of concept), Task 4 Training and User Manual, Task 5 Draft Report and Research Summary, and Task 6 Final Report, Research Summary and Presentation.
Task 2 requires a thorough literature search and review of other state DOT practices using AI/ML for right-of-way purposes.
Task 3c requires the Offeror to demonstrate how the technology creates draft legal land descriptions on a variety of properties, with MoDOT reviewing the drafts and giving improvement feedback.
Task 4 requires the Offeror to train Right of Way staff on the finalized system and supply a user manual for staff reference.
The contract period is 15 months, with the project schedule estimated to start November 1, 2024 and the final invoice due and contract ending February 2, 2026.

The proposal must include a Work Plan of no more than ten pages (12-point font minimum, excluding forms and resumes) describing how the Offeror will work with MoDOT to fulfill the project-specific requirements.
Proposals are due by email to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov at 10 a.m. Central on August 21, 2024, with notification of receipt sent by noon the same day.

Questions and comments must be submitted to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by 4 p.m. Central on July 17, 2024, and contacting MoDOT employees by any other method is prohibited and cause for disqualification.
MoDOT posts its responses to questions publicly on July 31, 2024, and notifies submitters about project selection or interviews on September 18, 2024.
Award goes to the Offeror providing the best proposal, with responsiveness determined first and proposals then evaluated against criteria established by the Technical Advisory Committee.
